verdict.rationale: Activepieces documents an API-key-authenticated public API and a built-in MCP server that lets AI assistants "build flows" and "drive the whole platform," so an agent can programmatically create flows. The evidence never shows specific API endpoints for creating, updating, or publishing flows, and the only documented activation path is the UI publish button. Missing for 10: documented flow create/update/publish endpoints in the public API, explicit evidence that agents can activate or publish flows programmatically, a published OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: Activepieces includes a built-in MCP server that lets AI assistants build flows, manage tables, test automations, and more — all through natural language.
Connect Claude, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client and it drives the whole platform.
The API uses "API keys" to authenticate requests.
you can pass the API key as a Bearer token in the header
